headline: An attacker rode 4,837 stolen GitHub accounts into more than 1,800 repositories to harvest continuous integration secrets and cloud keys, while fresh attacks through ScreenConnect extensions and N-able N-central turned remote management software into a highway to hundreds of customer machines.

emerging_trends.text: Developer identity now outranks server access as a prize: the wfx-loot campaign shows how one batch of stolen GitHub logins converts into continuous integration secrets that unlock cloud accounts, package registries, and production systems.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen GitHub Accounts Seed a Secret Stealer

emerging_trends.text: ConnectWise and N-able both spent the day fighting live intrusions through their own management platforms, the shortest route an attacker has to hundreds of downstream customers at once.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ScreenConnect and N-central Attacks Reach Customer Endpoints

emerging_trends.text: Darktrace drove Claude Code through Anthropic's own API with stolen keys, and separate crews keep GSocket running on Linux servers their victims already patched—attackers increasingly operate inside the tools and traffic defenders expect to see.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen Claude Keys Turn Claude Code Into an Implant

topics.title: ScreenConnect and N-central Attacks Reach Customer Endpoints
topics.latest_developments: ConnectWise disabled five third-party ScreenConnect extensions in partner environments after attackers exploited a flaw in one legitimate extension to walk past ScreenConnect authentication and push rogue remote-access clients onto at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations, and the company says it sees no compromise of its own infrastructure and no vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself; SecurityWeek reported that attacks on N-able N-central began shortly after a researcher published more than 30 zero-days, and that N-able's hotfixes close the ones an unauthenticated attacker can reach.
topics.summary: Both products are remote monitoring and management platforms that managed service providers use to administer client machines, which gives one compromised instance reach into every customer it serves. Administrators should apply N-able's hotfixes, check which ScreenConnect extensions their environment loads, and hunt for unexpected remote-access clients on managed endpoints.

sources.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
Hackers Deploy Malware in Fresh ScreenConnect Campaign
Hackers Target N-central Zero-Days as N-able Rushes Patches
Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations

topics.title: HTTP/2 and Pre-Auth Flaws Hit Core Server Software
topics.latest_developments: The Apache Software Foundation fixed CVE-2026-119618, a critical remote code execution flaw in the mod_http2 module that affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, in version 2.4.71 on November 11, 2026, and Red Hat, which ships the server with Red Hat Enterprise Linux, says only hosts with HTTP/2 enabled face exposure; Node.js closed 16 flaws in versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1, two of them in built-in HTTP/2 support that let an unauthenticated client crash a 24.x or 26.x server or pull back pieces of server memory holding other connections' responses; MongoDB patched CVE-2026-118383, which lets an unauthenticated attacker send two requests that crash a lagging replica set member once it takes over as primary; and Red Hat patched a critical Quay flaw that lets attackers steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and hold persistent access.
topics.summary: These are the web servers, runtimes, databases, and registries sitting under most enterprise applications, and three of the four flaws need no credentials at all. Inventory internet-facing Apache and Node.js hosts with HTTP/2 turned on, patch to 2.4.71 and the fixed Node.js lines, and update MongoDB replica set members and Quay registries.

sources.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data
Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover
Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images

topics.title: GSocket Keeps Linux Servers Owned After Patching
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented multiple threat actors planting GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, on compromised Linux servers to hold encrypted command and control after the victim patches the vulnerability that let the attacker in, and published detection, investigation, and remediation steps; the threat intelligence company Flare reported separately that underground forums now trade eBPF rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits that hide activity on Linux without loading a kernel module.
topics.summary: Patching an exploited flaw closes the door the attacker used and leaves the attacker inside, because GSocket rides outbound encrypted connections that look like administrative traffic. After any Linux server compromise, hunt for GSocket processes, unexpected cron and systemd persistence, and eBPF programs loaded outside your own tooling.

sources.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice

topics.title: Poland Pulls ePUAP Offline as Japan Funds Responders
topics.latest_developments: Poland shut down ePUAP, the nationwide platform citizens use to file official documents, correspond with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online, after a cyberattack; Japan's emergency cybersecurity package adds public-private cyber responders and an AI-focused team run by the economy ministry, plus wider latitude to use the government's new active cyber-defense powers, a response to AI-assisted breaches at dozens of Japanese companies and agencies; and Britain and France issued the first joint guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capability vendors, calling on firms that build, sell, or finance the tools to vet customers, build technical safeguards against misuse, and run systems for monitoring and reporting abuse.
topics.summary: Three governments moved the same week on national cyber exposure, one by taking a citizen-facing service down and two by funding and regulating. Organizations filing through ePUAP should expect outages, and spyware vendors selling into Britain or France now face a written customer due diligence standard.

sources.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms

topics.title: Stolen GitHub Accounts Seed a Secret Stealer
topics.latest_developments: Aikido Security disclosed a campaign it calls wfx-loot, in which an attacker holding stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts pushed a credential-stealing payload into tens of thousands of repositories starting Tuesday, November 10, 2026, and ran it in at least 1,806 of them, shipping GitHub Actions secrets and cloud credentials back out; the compromised accounts also opened probe pull requests across the repositories they could write to.
topics.summary: GitHub Actions workflows carry the secrets that reach cloud accounts, container registries, and production systems, so every secret the malware touched counts as burned. Anyone whose repositories accepted commits or workflow runs since November 10, 2026 should rotate Actions secrets and cloud credentials, revoke tokens, and audit recent pull requests and commit authors.

sources.title: Check your GitHub repos: A secret stealer hit tens of thousands of them
Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories

topics.title: Stolen Claude Keys Turn Claude Code Into an Implant
topics.latest_developments: Darktrace researchers showed in a lab test that an attacker holding a stolen Claude API key can run Claude Code as a remote-controlled implant, steering the coding agent through the memory stores feature of Anthropic's platform and pulling a one-gigabyte file out through the Claude Files API, with every task and every result traveling to api.anthropic.com, the same endpoint the agent already calls for inference; Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, published mitigations the same day for attacker use of AI red team tools including ARTEX.
topics.summary: A coding agent already installed and trusted on a developer workstation becomes the command channel, and its traffic blends into ordinary agent activity that network monitoring treats as benign. Treat Claude API keys as production credentials, rotate exposed ones, and watch for agent sessions that no developer started.

sources.title: Stolen Claude API keys can turn Claude Code into a remote-controlled implant
ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know

business_politics.title: Nvidia's Board Moves to Oust Huang
business_politics.latest_developments: Nvidia shares fell 7% ahead of Thursday's Wall Street open, November 12, as the board gathered to settle Jensen Huang's fate following a report of a second affair, and Beijing warned Washington against treating the scandal as a pretext for new chip restrictions.
business_politics.summary: Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and built it into the supplier of the chips behind the artificial-intelligence boom, faces removal after the company's own investigation into his affair with a Chinese woman whom United States intelligence identifies as a spy, and the Financial Times reported a second relationship with a subordinate at the company. The leadership crisis knocked Nasdaq futures down 1% and pulled Asian equities lower, and The Economist judged that Huang's recklessness leaves the board no good options; China's government accuses Washington of fabricating espionage narratives.

sources.title: Nvidia Is Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang

business_politics.title: Witkoff and Kushner Carry the Abu Dhabi Result to Putin
business_politics.latest_developments: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow Thursday, November 12, to put the results of the Abu Dhabi negotiations to Vladimir Putin, and Ukraine said restrictions on its military Starlink service have returned.
business_politics.summary: The Kyiv and Moscow delegations agreed in Abu Dhabi only to a large prisoner exchange, and President Trump's envoys now take the question of a ceasefire directly to Putin while European capitals argue over who among them should speak to him. Ukrainian commanders say drones running on Starshield, the military version of SpaceX's Starlink, lose connectivity above 100 miles an hour, which cripples their interception of Russia's jet-powered drones.

sources.title: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions are back as US envoys land in Moscow

business_politics.title: Tehran Sets Terms for Reopening Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: Crude fell Thursday, November 12, as traders weighed renewed United States-Iran diplomacy against the conditions Tehran attaches to reopening the Strait of Hormuz and the continuing threats to regional shipping.
business_politics.summary: The war between the United States and Iran shut the strait that carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, and the price of crude now turns on Tehran's terms. The Financial Times reported that Russian diesel exports doubled after Trump lifted sanctions on Moscow, with none of the cargo reaching American buyers, and Ukraine's resumed strikes on Russian refineries should cut that flow back.

sources.title: Oil Prices Fall as Investors Weigh U.S.-Iran Diplomacy
Russian diesel exports double after Trump lifts sanctions, but US gets none

business_politics.title: France Backs Spain's Candidate for the ECB
business_politics.latest_developments: Paris signaled Thursday, November 12, that it will support Pablo Hernandez de Cos, Spain's candidate to become the next president of the European Central Bank.
business_politics.summary: France and Germany are assembling a package deal on central bank leadership, and the French signal gives momentum to the Spanish bid for the job that sets monetary policy for the 20 countries of the euro area.

sources.title: France signals support for Spain's ECB presidential candidate

business.title: The Money Gap in Downtown Conversions
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette put numbers Thursday, November 12, on the gap between what an office-to-apartment conversion costs downtown and what the finished rents support, using the Gulf Tower as its case.
business.summary: Apartments in Pittsburgh's Golden Triangle keep filling while the office towers around them empty, and the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership's figures show conversion economics that fall short without subsidy. Mayor Corey O'Connor's administration and downtown landlords both need the math to work to keep the Golden Triangle's tax base intact.

sources.title: Balancing Downtown Pittsburgh's office market with residential conversions reveals a money gap

business.title: Monroeville Mall's Last Christmas
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Thursday, November 12, that Monroeville Mall may be hosting its final holiday shopping season.
business.summary: The enclosed mall on Route 22 in Monroeville, Allegheny County, has anchored eastern suburban retail for decades, and its tenants now face the prospect of shutting down after Christmas.

sources.title: Is this the last holiday shopping season at Monroeville Mall?

business.title: Pittsburgh's Leverage Over UPMC and Highmark
business.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Brandon McGinley argued Thursday, November 12, that Pittsburgh may finally hold real leverage over its largest tax-exempt nonprofits.
business.summary: UPMC and Highmark own much of the city's most valuable real estate and pay no property tax on it, and Mayor Corey O'Connor opened his term facing a projected $250 million deficit over five years. McGinley weighed the city's options on payments in lieu of taxes and on challenging charitable exemptions outright.

sources.title: Brandon McGinley: Does Pittsburgh finally have real leverage against major nonprofits?

around_town.title: Red Light Cameras Issue 10,000 Warnings
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's red light cameras produced more than 10,000 warnings in their first 60 days of enforcement, KDKA reported Thursday, November 12.
around_town.summary: The city is running its new camera program in a warning phase before it starts mailing fines. KDKA's John Shumway reported that cities typically see these totals spike at the start and fall off as drivers learn where the cameras sit.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's red light camera enforcement results in more than 10,000 warnings in first 60 days

around_town.title: Shapiro Restates His Case for the Popular Vote
around_town.latest_developments: Governor Josh Shapiro told PublicSource in a story published Thursday, November 12, that "the national popular vote makes sense" and that he will work with lawmakers on a mechanism for it.
around_town.summary: Democrats took unified control of more state governments in the November 3 elections, including both chambers in Harrisburg, which puts electoral college changes within reach of legislatures that can direct how their states award presidential electors. Pennsylvania carries 19 electoral votes and decides presidential elections.

sources.title: Democrats have gained control in more states. That could change the way the U.S. elects its president.

around_town.title: Deluzio Collects Chits Against Fetterman
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, November 12, that Representative Chris Deluzio of Aspinwall campaigned for Democrats who won last week, and that those allies could line up behind a primary challenge to Senator John Fetterman in 2028.
around_town.summary: Fetterman has alienated much of the Pennsylvania Democratic Party, and Governor Josh Shapiro told him publicly on November 8 to repair the damage. Deluzio, a second-term congressman from Allegheny County, has emerged as the party figure best positioned to use the goodwill he banked in the midterms.

sources.title: Rep. Chis Deluzio helped fellow Democrats win last week. They could return the favor against John Fetterman in 2028

events.title: Jack White Headlines the Weekend
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its weekend guide Thursday, November 12, led by a Jack White concert, a Rush anniversary show, and Brazilian jazz.
events.summary: The guide collects the weekend of November 13 through November 15 in Pittsburgh around those three music bills, with the former White Stripes frontman topping the list.

sources.title: Things to do this weekend in Pittsburgh: Jack White in concert, Rush at 50-something, Brazilian jazz, more

events.title: City Paper's Week: Emo, Quilts, and Greek Tragedy
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published its calendar Thursday, November 12, for Thursday, November 12, through Wednesday, November 18.
events.summary: The week's list runs a secret emo show, a quilt sew-a-long, an operatic staging of a Greek tragedy, and a post-apocalyptic musical across Pittsburgh venues.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's top events: Thu., Nov. 12-Wed., Nov. 18

events.title: Riverfront Theater Stages 'Spring Awakening'
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Thursday, November 12, that Riverfront Theater Company closes its 2026 season with the rock musical "Spring Awakening."
events.summary: The show, adapted from Frank Wedekind's play, tells a story of adolescent revolt and self-discovery and carries a reputation for jarring its audiences.

sources.title: Riverfront Theater Company staging poignant story of youth revolt with 'Spring Awakening'

events.title: Sarah Kramer Takes Over Attack Theatre
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled Sarah Kramer on Thursday, November 12, as she begins directing Attack Theatre.
events.summary: Kramer came to the Pittsburgh dance company from the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, and she brings that programming experience to a troupe known for pairing contemporary dance with live music in unconventional spaces.

sources.title: Attack Theatre's new director combines her early love of dance with Kennedy Center experience

around_teams.title: Tomlin on Retiring and Working for NBC
around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football released part two of Cam Heyward's interview with Mike Tomlin at 6 a.m. Eastern Thursday, November 12, in which the former Steelers head coach walks through his retirement decision and his new job at NBC.
around_teams.summary: Tomlin coached the Steelers for 18 seasons before stepping away, and he sat down with Heyward and co-host Hayden for a two-part conversation; part one, posted Tuesday, November 10, covered Ben Roethlisberger, Aaron Rodgers, and how Tomlin got the job in 2007.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward

around_teams.title: The Pirates Measure the Gap to Milwaukee and Tampa Bay
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, November 12, that the Pirates came out of Major League Baseball's general managers meetings acknowledging a "significant gap" between themselves and the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays.
around_teams.summary: General manager Ben Cherington said this week that Pittsburgh holds the payroll flexibility to add this winter, with Rays infielder Brandon Lowe among the names in play. The Brewers and Rays are the small-market clubs the Pirates measure themselves against, and closing on them sets the standard for the offseason.

sources.title: The Pirates hope to close the 'significant gap' between themselves and the Brewers and Rays

team_usa.title: Manchester United Fires Carrick, Closes on Pochettino
team_usa.latest_developments: Manchester United sacked head coach Michael Carrick on Thursday, November 12, with the club sitting in the relegation zone, and sources told ESPN that United States men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is close to replacing him.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino has led the United States since 2024 and carries a $10 million release clause, and he has spoken of wanting to return to European club work; he took over Carrick's predecessor's squad talk 10 months after Carrick won the Old Trafford job. ESPN's analysts laid out who could take the national team into the 2027 Gold Cup and beyond, with the November Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti already on the calendar.

team_usa.title: The U.S. Bid for 2031 Clears FIFA's Review
team_usa.latest_developments: FIFA found Thursday, November 12, that the United States-led bid for the 2031 Women's World Cup and the United Kingdom bid for 2035 both meet hosting requirements, sending them to a vote of the member federations later this month.
team_usa.summary: U.S. Soccer leads a joint North American bid for 2031 and runs unopposed, which puts the women's tournament on American fields five years after the 2026 men's World Cup. The membership votes before the end of November.

sources.title: U.S.-led, UK bids for Women's World Cup cleared for FIFA vote
